questions.q: Why is detecting flash crashes and data errors usually treated as anomaly detection rather than supervised classification?
options: Classification algorithms cannot run on financial data
Labeled examples of crashes/errors are rare, heterogeneous, and the next event likely won't resemble past ones
Anomaly detection is always more accurate than classification
Regulators require anomaly detection specifically for compliance
questions.explain: Crashes and data errors are rare and don't repeat identically, so there isn't a reliable labeled dataset for a classifier to generalize from. Unsupervised anomaly detection instead asks whether an observation fits the normal distribution of the data.

questions.q: What is the core intuition behind IsolationForest flagging a point as anomalous?
options: It computes the Euclidean distance to the nearest cluster centroid
Outlier points tend to get isolated into their own leaf in unusually few random tree splits
It requires labeled anomaly examples to train each tree
It fits a single Gaussian distribution to the entire dataset
questions.explain: IsolationForest builds random trees; points far from the dense bulk of normal data tend to split off into their own leaf quickly. Averaging this isolation speed across trees produces an anomaly score.

questions.q: What does the contamination parameter in IsolationForest or EllipticEnvelope control?
options: The number of trees in the forest
The assumed fraction of the data that is anomalous, which sets the decision threshold
The kernel used to transform features
The number of PCA components retained
questions.explain: contamination is a prior on what proportion of observations are expected to be anomalous; it directly determines where the anomaly/normal decision boundary is drawn.

questions.q: What assumption does EllipticEnvelope make about the data that OneClassSVM does not?
options: That the data is labeled
That the data has no outliers at all
That the normal data roughly follows a single Gaussian distribution, fit via a robust covariance estimate
That the data must first be reduced with PCA
questions.explain: EllipticEnvelope fits one robust Gaussian ellipse to the data and flags points far from its center, which is a poor fit if the data is multi-modal or spans multiple regimes. OneClassSVM instead learns a more flexible boundary.

questions.q: Which of these is a realistic practical use of market anomaly detection described in the lesson?
options: Predicting next quarter's earnings per share
Flagging a price print inconsistent with recent trading as a possible feed error before it reaches a risk system
Replacing the need for any supervised return-prediction model
Automatically executing trades with no human review
questions.explain: A common real use is catching bad prints, stale data, or liquidity-event days as candidates for review before they corrupt a risk system, backtest, or live signal.
